# 1 Chronicles Chapter 26 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 383v–384r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_026_page_001.jpg, 1CH_026_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites — Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the descendants of Asaph. **2** Meshelemiah's sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, **3** Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.

**4** Obed-edom's sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth, **5** Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth — because God had blessed him.

**6** Shemaiah's sons were born as leaders of their father's household, because they were exceptionally capable men. **7** Shemaiah's sons: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, along with his capable relatives Elihu and Semachiah. **8** All of these belonged to Obed-edom's family — they, their sons, and their relatives were strong, capable men fit for service. Obed-edom's family totaled sixty-two.

**9** Meshelemiah had sons and relatives who were capable men — eighteen in all. **10** Hosah, from the line of Merari, had sons: Shimri was the chief — although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him to lead — **11** Hilkiah was second, Tebaliah third, Zechariah fourth. Hosah's sons and relatives totaled thirteen.

**12** These divisions of gatekeepers, organized by their leading men, had assigned duties for serving in the LORD's temple, just like their relatives. **13** They cast lots for each gate, family by family, without regard to seniority.

**14** The lot for the east gate fell to Shelemiah. Then they cast lots for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and his lot came up for the north gate. **15** Obed-edom received the south gate, and his sons were assigned the storehouse. **16** Shuppim and Hosah received the west, at the Shalleketh Gate on the upper road — one guard post facing another.

**17** The daily deployment: six Levites at the east; four at the north; four at the south; two pairs at the storehouse; **18** and at the western court, four on the road and two in the court itself.

**19** These were the gatekeeping divisions from the families of Korah and Merari.

**20** Fellow Levites were placed in charge of the temple treasuries and the treasuries for dedicated gifts. **21** From the descendants of Ladan the Gershonite, the family heads were led by Jehieli. **22** Jehieli's sons, Zetham and his brother Joel, were responsible for the treasuries of the LORD's temple.

**23** From the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites: **24** Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the chief officer over the treasuries. **25** His relatives through the line of Eliezer: Rehabiah, then Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomith. **26** Shelomith and his relatives were in charge of all the treasuries holding the items dedicated by King David, the family heads, and the military commanders of all ranks.

**27** They had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to maintain the LORD's temple. **28** Everything dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah — all consecrated items were entrusted to Shelomith and his relatives.

**29** From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were assigned responsibilities outside the temple — serving as officials and judges throughout Israel. **30** From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives — 1,700 capable men — supervised everything west of the Jordan related to the LORD's work and the king's service.

**31** Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites. In the fortieth year of David's reign, a search of the genealogical records found capable men from this family at Jazer in Gilead. **32** David appointed 2,700 of Jerijah's capable relatives, all family heads, over the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh — to handle every matter pertaining to God and the king.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 5 — "because God had blessed him":** This brief note carries enormous backstory. Obed-edom was the man who housed the ark of God after Uzzah's death (2 Sam 6:10-12). The LORD's blessing on his household became legendary — and here it manifests as eight sons, all of them strong and capable, producing a family line of sixty-two temple servants. The ark's blessing bore generational fruit.

**Verse 10 — "although he was not the firstborn":** A recurring biblical theme — God (and godly fathers) often bypass the firstborn. Shimri was appointed chief over his older brothers, echoing the stories of Isaac over Ishmael, Jacob over Esau, David over his brothers.

**Verse 27 — "plunder from battles":** War spoil became sacred treasure. The Chronicler traces a direct line from the battlefield to the temple treasury — violence transformed into worship, the spoils of conflict funding the house of peace.

*— PNEUMA*
